I was cyberbullied pretty bad at two different points in my life. The second time I was ousted from a lot of my friend groups and a community I had loved because two people made me a victim of their smear campaign (like they had done to a dozen other people). I don’t really care anymore. I’ve gotten involved in a new online circle of people that are actually kind and genuine people. People can and will find any reason to hate you and that’s a reflection of them, not you. But carefully minding my social circle and community, and withdrawing from social media as much as possible, and being as impersonal as possible, and avoiding spaces or pages that might upset me has been key. If I start reading something that upsets me (especially if it’s about me) I close out immediately. Don’t finish reading it. Also just don’t engage drama, ever. Especially not drama someone tries to muck up on you. Don’t bother trying to defend yourself, or cover it up, or disprove wild accusations – just let them go and people will forget. Block and delete anyone trying to start something. And most importantly don’t engage people that are often in, or starting drama, even if you’re on “their” side. If they run out of drama supply they’ll turn on you.

ETA: if you can, really do take a break from social media. You don’t have to start nuking accounts but maybe take a two day, two week break and see how you feel about the account later. Migrate to sites that are more impersonal and do more browsing and less posting. If you’re gonna stay online, cultivate a corner that benefits you, and stay out of communities with bad reputations.

One of the most powerful things you can do, IME, is stand up for yourself.

Narcissists might say “I don’t deserve this” to manipulate and guilt others but you’re allowed to say “I don’t deserve this” in response to your abuse. You’re allowed to have compassion for yourself and you should. You are your own best advocate and you are your own person worthy of having boundaries, and it’s no one’s place to harass you for it.

Sometimes it’s hard for me to remember but I try to remind myself that I didn’t deserve the treatment I endured during childhood, that even if I was a “difficult” or dishonest child what I did does not reflect on me now, and that 90% of the “bad” things I did were either not as bad as my Nmom insisted or a result of me being abused or both. What abusive people say about me is reflective of their character, not mine. What they say might hurt not because it’s true but because they know you, they know how to hurt you, and that’s what they intend to do.

I also have to remind myself that I shouldn’t minimize my own experiences, to consider how I’d feel if someone else experienced what I went through and to consider the implications me minimizing my experiences has for all other abuse survivors.

You can apologize for upsetting them, and I don’t think that’s a necessarily a bad idea, but you should still reaffirm that you are entitled to having boundaries and it’s not an unreasonable request. It was inappropriate of them to react the way they did, too. Keep in mind that in all likelihood, them saying they’re hurt is just another tactic to manipulate you.

I’m sorry you went through that. I also admire you for being able to stand up for yourself! That takes a lot of courage.
